claim.hypothesis: P is a minimum-order counterexample among all finite 2-groups to the cyclic subgroup TPP order inequality, with distinguished factors <a>,<b>,<c>.
conclusions: P/P⁴ has the explicit order-32 presentation given in section 3.
Every Frattini iterate equals the corresponding ordinary power subgroup; from P⁸ downward the three marked cyclic power factors give genuinely bijective ordered coordinates.
claim.scope: Necessary conditions only; no unrestricted 2-group cyclic TPP resolution.

new_elementary_lemmas: If N is normal in a finite 2-group G, N<=G² and [N,G]<=N², then [N,G²]<=N⁴ and N is powerful.
In dimensions at most two, the stated spanning square-action identities force both actions to be trivial.

retained_input_boundary.rank_three_obstruction: Elementary reductions, binary square-action lemma, powerful-Frattini obstruction; no isobicyclic classification needed.
retained_input_boundary.index_256_powerful_P8: Also uses the previously proved minimum-factor-at-least-eight consequence of the marked-isobicyclic classification. That input is retained, not eliminated.
retained_input_boundary.deep_coordinates: Published powerful-group ordered-factorization and power-subgroup structure retained through phase11.

computation.top_coordinate_shortcut: Explicit pair of commuting binary involutions refutes the weaker fixed-coordinate inference.

limits: Some marked eighth-power factors may be trivial.
No product-map injectivity is assumed before the powerful ordered-factorization argument.
No equality of iterated square subgroups and ordinary powers is assumed; the relevant equalities are proved.
A fixed line in the final linear action need not be a marked coordinate line.
No full Lean formalization or new Lean module.
Full cyclic TPP for finite 2-groups remains unresolved.
